drivingQuestion: Was the man's or the woman's case obvious to R' Yohanan ben Nuri?
outcomeNote: dilemma raised; addressed in the next unit

segments.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי וְכוּ׳. אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ? רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן נוּרִי, אִישׁ פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, וְאִשָּׁה קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ. אוֹ דִלְמָא: אִשָּׁה פְּשִׁיטָא לֵיהּ, וְאִישׁ קָמִיבַּעְיָא לֵיהּ.
segments.en: § The mishna taught that «Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri said:» What is the reason that the husband of a woman who became a deaf-mute may divorce her, whereas a man who becomes a deaf-mute may not divorce his wife? «A dilemma was raised before» the scholars with regard to the opinion of «Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Nuri:» Is it «obvious to him» that a deaf-mute «man» may not divorce his wife, «and he raised» his «dilemma» with regard to «a woman,» i.e., why she may be divorced if she is a deaf-mute? «Or perhaps,» it is «obvious to him» why one may divorce a deaf-mute «woman, and he raised» his «dilemma» with regard to a deaf-mute «man,» i.e., why he may not divorce his wife.
